newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Pliva up 2 pct on '96 results.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Pliva up 2 pct on '96 results.

text.p: Leading Croatian drugs firm Pliva rose over two percent in heavy trade on Friday, following its good 1996 business results, traders said.
It gained 10 kuna to 489, trading over 4,000 shares on the Zagreb Stock Exchange by noon local time (1000 gmt), a trader told Reuters.
"Pliva went up, but it did not go crazy. The results were good, but they were already calculated into the price," Josko Milisa of I.C.F. brokerage told Reuters.
Pliva said on Friday it 1996 net profit went up 14.39 percent to 456 million kuna, while pre-tax profit grew 30.9 percent to 616 million.
In London, Pliva earlier reached $16.2 per GDR, issued five for each share, but fell back to $15.875 shortly after the release of the 1996 results. -- Davor Huic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
